measured.hook_rotation: episode hook 5 Bold Statement, previous episode hook 4, format 1 In This Town, previous was not a story format: ok

notes.hook: Line 1 is a rule statement ('In this town, being kind will cost you everything you're wearing') more than a truly bold or controversial claim. It is the TeamDeam 'In this town...' opener with a mild kindness-is-dangerous twist, so it passes rotation (bold claim about the world) but is not shocking. 'everything' also overstates: the rule only takes one accessory per kind act. First shot is a static grey wide aerial with no character, no motion and no action, so the hook is weak visually.
notes.structure: All TeamDeam-pattern elements are present: rule + 3 examples + 'because of this', outsider with secret, strange first consequence, mentor with the refused fix, wider escalation, mystery trail, stacked reveals (sister, scarf), resolution through the theme, mentor twist, sequel-hook chest. Several are present but not fully earned: see fixes.
notes.originality: Premise (kindness moves your accessory; thanks returns it brighter) is original and not close to TeamDeam titles (lie->animal, 10 jumps, golden gift except me). Pattern is copied only structurally, which the framework allows. Not web-searched; the research agent's search found no overlap.

fixes: Lines 25-32 / 34 (cellar and Lena logic): the shelves of hats, scarves and glasses in the Lost and Found are unexplained. Under the world rule, accessories jump onto the helped person, not into a cellar. Also unexplained: the tiny red hat trail (Milo's cap went to Pip), why Pip runs to the cellar (line 33), and how the town knows to thank Lena (line 39). Add one line each, e.g. Lena collects the things people drop, leaves a trail of her own small gifts, and the town learns it was her from the trail. Also drop the research beat where Lena does not recognise Milo or use it; the script loses that emotional beat.

Lines 1, 2-4 (hook and rule examples): make the opener sharper and the premise payoff tighter. Change 'everything you're wearing' to match the rule ('one thing every time'), or make the opener a real controversial claim ('In this town, being kind is the worst thing you can do.'). Make shot 1 show colour being taken (a hat flying off a grey crowd) instead of a static wide, and spend motion budget on shots 2-4 (the three rule examples are stills of mid-air transfers, which image-to-video should show) instead of the glow and sparkle shots.

Lines 12 and 17 (open loops never closed, escalation stalls): Milo's hair glowing gold and Milo having a body full of accessories are never explained or paid off, and Tilda's warning ('you would end up like her') has no demonstrated stakes. Pay off the glow (kindness gives light; it flares when he helps, and again when thanked), and have Tilda show the cost (she explains the rule, and her bare hands). Lines 20-24 (fight, hiding, empty square) are told, not shown: 'the town started to fight' is vague, so replace it with a concrete beat, such as the baker refusing Pip's thanks or two neighbours dodging each other's help.

Producibility fixes: line 34 ('at night with a lantern') uses the Town square look that says 'bright game daylight', so the generated image will be daytime. Override the lighting for night/sunset in shots 34 and 24-26 and the cellar. Line 9 and the lighthouse cellar door use 'LOST AND FOUND' text although the style line says 'no text': remove the sign text (use a lantern icon or a plain crate) or accept that text will be garbled. The shot character key is 'Baker' but the character name is 'The baker'; make them match. Lena, Pip and Tilda are all grey-on-grey like the Townsfolk, so give each one fixed colour-free identifiers (Lena two brown pigtails and a lantern; Pip bandage; Tilda cane) in every shot and keep them in frame.

Title/description: title 'In This Town, Being Kind Costs You Your Clothes... #Shorts' is on pattern and good, but 'Clothes' is not what the story says (accessories), so use 'Costs You Everything You're Wearing...' or 'Your Hat'. The description line 3 spoils the sister reveal; cut it to 'A boy keeps helping a town that forgot kindness.' CTA is good. Add #roblox #robloxstory to the first line of hashtags and keep the 'not affiliated' line.
kid_safety: Pass. No violence, no real people, no brand assets (the disclaimer is present). The 'fight' beat is angry faces only; keep it that way.
